issues.legal_issue: A statutory right of pre-emption survives the pre-emptor’s death and may be pursued by legal representatives who succeed to the relevant rights by inheritance.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought statutory pre-emption suits based on his relationship to the vendor, and decrees were granted and affirmed on first appeal.
The plaintiff died while second appeals were pending, and his legal representatives were brought on record.
The claim concerned agricultural land and depended on the statutory qualifications governing the pre-emptor and the vendor.
issues.conclusion: The right to sue did not abate on the plaintiff’s death, and his legal representatives were properly brought on record in the pending appeals.
issues.legal_principle: The statutory right of pre-emption is not an interest in land, but it attaches to the land and is enforceable against a purchaser. Although the right is personal in the sense that it depends on the pre-emptor’s relationship with the vendor, a successor who takes the relevant land by inheritance takes the rights that go with it. The Court relied on section 306 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, and Order XXII, rules 1 and 11, read with rule 10, of the Code of Civil Procedure. It approved Faqir Ali Shah v. Rani Kishan, 133 P.R. 1907, and Wajid Ali v. Shaban, I.L.R. 31 All. 623; it distinguished the rule concerning pre-emption under Mohammedan law discussed in Muhammad Husain v. Niamat-un-nissa, I.L.R. 20 All. 88.

rule.if: statutory_preemption_proceeding and qualifying_preemption_relationship and preemptor_dies_while_appeal_pending and legal_representatives_succeed_by_inheritance

predicates.statutory_preemption_proceeding: A claimant brings a proceeding to enforce a statutory right of pre-emption.
predicates.qualifying_preemption_relationship: The claimant and vendor have the relationship and other statutory qualifications on which the asserted pre-emption right depends.
predicates.preemptor_dies_while_appeal_pending: The claimant dies while an appeal in the pre-emption proceeding remains pending.
predicates.legal_representatives_succeed_by_inherit: The claimant’s legal representatives succeed by inheritance to the relevant estate or land rights.

issues.definition: When a qualified claimant pursues statutory pre-emption, dies during a pending appeal, and is succeeded by inheritance, the claim survives to the legal representatives.

issues.legal_issue: A retrospective amendment does not bar a decree for successors where the claimant’s right of pre-emption existed under the law applicable when the suit was instituted and the right was not extinguished by the claimant’s death.
material_facts: The sales and the suits occurred after the amending legislation had come into force.
The claimant’s asserted right fell within the amended law when he instituted the suits.
The claimant died while appeals were pending, but the right to sue survived to his legal representatives.
issues.conclusion: The amended Act did not bar a decree in favour of the substituted legal representatives because the claimant’s right existed when he instituted the suits and passed to them on his death.
issues.legal_principle: Section 31 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913, as amended by Punjab Act 10 of 1960, did not bar relief on these facts: the claimant sued after the amendment and had a right under the amended Act at that time, and that right survived his death. Ram Sarup v. Munshi, [1963] 3 S.C.R. 858, was distinguishable because the amendment there retrospectively extinguished the plaintiff’s asserted right, whereas it did not extinguish the right asserted in this case.

rule.if: statutory_preemption_proceeding and suit_instituted_after_amendment and claimant_qualified_under_law_at_filing and claim_survives_claimant_death

predicates.statutory_preemption_proceeding: A claimant brings a proceeding to enforce a statutory right of pre-emption.
predicates.suit_instituted_after_amendment: The claimant institutes the suit after a change in the governing law has come into force.
predicates.claimant_qualified_under_law_at_filing: The claimant’s asserted right falls within the law applicable when the suit is instituted.
predicates.claim_survives_claimant_death: The claimant’s right to sue continues after death and passes to the legal representatives.

issues.definition: If a claimant sues after a legal change, qualifies under the law then applicable, and the claim survives the claimant’s death, the change does not bar a decree for the successors.
